theme: The American Revolution: Independence & Founding Era
title: The American Revolution: Independence & Founding Era
description: A 60-question grand master assessment on the 1776 Declaration of Independence, Continental Army, Boston Tea Party, Yorktown, the Founding Fathers, and the US Constitution.

questions.question: What British parliamentary act of 1765 levied direct taxes on all colonial paper goods, sparking widespread protests of no taxation without representation?
questions.explanation: The Stamp Act unified colonial opposition across all thirteen colonies, leading to the Stamp Act Congress and eventual repeal.

questions.question: What deadly 1770 confrontation in Boston saw British soldiers fire into an unruly crowd, killing five colonists including Crispus Attucks?
questions.explanation: Patriot leader Samuel Adams and engraver Paul Revere publicized the event as a massacre to galvanize anti-British sentiment.

questions.question: What famous political protest in December 1773 involved the Sons of Liberty dumping 342 chests of British East India Company tea into Boston Harbor?
questions.explanation: Protesting the Tea Act monopoly, disguised colonists boarded three merchant vessels and destroyed over 92,000 pounds of tea.

questions.question: What punitive legislation did Parliament pass in 1774 in response to the Boston Tea Party, known in Britain as the Coercive Acts?
questions.explanation: The Intolerable Acts closed Boston Port, suspended the Massachusetts colonial charter, and mandated the housing of British troops.

questions.question: Where did delegates from twelve of the thirteen colonies convene in September 1774 to coordinate collective colonial resistance?
questions.explanation: Meeting at Carpenters Hall in Philadelphia, delegates established the Continental Association boycott of British trade.

questions.question: How many chests of British East India Company tea were destroyed during the Boston Tea Party on December 16, 1773?
questions.explanation: Colonial protestors destroyed 342 chests containing over 46 tons of imported tea valued at roughly 10,000 British pounds.

questions.question: What military encounters on April 19, 1775, sparked the armed conflict of the American Revolutionary War with the shot heard round the world?
questions.explanation: British troops marching to seize militia weapons caches clashed with colonial minutemen on Lexington Green and Concords North Bridge.

questions.question: Which Boston silversmith made a famous midnight ride on April 18, 1775, to warn Samuel Adams and John Hancock that British regulars were advancing?
questions.explanation: Revere coordinated two lanterns hung in the Old North Church steeple before riding westward toward Concord.

questions.question: In which June 1775 battle did colonial militia inflict heavy casualties on British forces attacking across Charlestown Peninsula before retreating?
questions.explanation: Fought primarily on Breeds Hill, the battle cost the British over 1,000 casualties and proved colonial troops could withstand regular forces.

questions.question: Who was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the newly created Continental Army by the Second Continental Congress in June 1775?
questions.explanation: George Washington took command of colonial forces surrounding Boston, establishing discipline and supply lines without accepting a salary.

questions.question: Which British-held Lake Champlain fortress was captured in May 1775 in a surprise dawn raid by Ethan Allen and Benedict Arnold?
questions.explanation: Heavy cannons captured at Fort Ticonderoga were later transported by Henry Knox across winter snow to fortify Dorchester Heights.

questions.question: What was the approximate riding distance in kilometers traveled by Paul Revere on his midnight ride from Charlestown to Lexington?
questions.explanation: Paul Revere rode roughly 20 kilometers through Somerville, Medford, and Arlington before reaching Lexington.

questions.question: What bestselling 47-page pamphlet published in January 1776 by Thomas Paine galvanized popular support for full independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: Common Sense sold hundreds of thousands of copies, using plain language to denounce hereditary monarchy and champion republican self-rule.

questions.question: Who was the primary author chosen by the Committee of Five to draft the United States Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Thomas Jefferson penned the draft in Philadelphia, drawing upon Enlightenment philosophy regarding fundamental natural rights.

questions.question: On what exact date did the Second Continental Congress formally adopt the final text of the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Congress voted for independence on July 2 and officially ratified the wording of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Continental Congress who famously inscribed the largest and most prominent signature on the Declaration?
questions.explanation: John Hancock signed with bold flourish so King George III could read his name without spectacles, making his name synonymous with a signature.

questions.question: What three unalienable rights are explicitly proclaimed in the preamble of the Declaration of Independence?
options: Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness
questions.explanation: Jefferson adapted John Locke concept of natural rights into life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness as self-evident truths.

questions.question: How many colonial delegates signed the official parchment copy of the United States Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Fifty-six delegates representing all thirteen colonies signed the document, pledging their lives, fortunes, and sacred honor.

questions.question: On Christmas night 1776, what icy river did George Washington lead his army across to launch a surprise attack on Trenton?
questions.explanation: Washington transported 2,400 men, artillery, and horses across the ice-choked Delaware River during a blizzard to assault the Hessian garrison.

questions.question: What German auxiliary mercenaries contracted by King George III were defeated and captured by Washington at the Battle of Trenton?
questions.explanation: Over 900 Hessian troops stationed in Trenton were caught off guard on the morning of December 26, 1776, revitalizing patriot morale.

questions.question: Following Trenton, what January 1777 battle saw Washington slip away in the night and outmaneuver British forces under Lord Cornwallis?
questions.explanation: At Princeton, Washington rallied retreating militia in person, securing his second vital victory in ten days and retaking New Jersey.

questions.question: Which American schoolteacher and spy was captured by the British in New York and executed in 1776, famously declaring he regretted having but one life to lose for his country?
questions.explanation: Nathan Hale was hanged without trial at age twenty-one, honored as America's first executed military intelligence officer.

questions.question: Which covert spy ring organized by Major Benjamin Tallmadge provided crucial intelligence from British-occupied New York to General Washington?
questions.explanation: Operating with invisible ink and numerical ciphers, the Culper Ring uncovered British naval plans and Benedict Arnold's treason.

questions.question: Approximately how many Hessian soldiers were captured as prisoners of war by Continental forces at the Battle of Trenton?
questions.explanation: Washington captured approximately 900 Hessian soldiers, six brass cannons, and vital supply wagons with minimal American casualties.

questions.question: Where did George Washington Continental Army endure a harsh winter encampment marked by disease, cold, and starvation during the winter of 1777 and 1778?
questions.explanation: Despite losing over 2,000 men to disease and exposure, the army emerged from Valley Forge transformed into a professional fighting force.

questions.question: Which Prussian military officer arrived at Valley Forge to institute standardized bayonet drills, discipline, and the Blue Book manual?
questions.explanation: Von Steuben created a model company of soldiers who trained the rest of the army in European linear tactics and rapid bayonet charges.

questions.question: Which 19-year-old French aristocrat volunteered to fight for the American cause, becoming a trusted general and surrogate son to Washington?
questions.explanation: Lafayette spent his own fortune to outfit American troops, served bravely at Brandywine, and secured crucial French military support.

questions.question: Which Polish military engineer constructed key river fortifications at West Point and Bemis Heights for the Continental Army?
questions.explanation: Kosciuszko's defensive earthworks were instrumental in winning the Battle of Saratoga and securing the Hudson River.

questions.question: Which Polish nobleman is celebrated as the Father of American Cavalry after reorganizing the Continental mounted forces before falling at Savannah?
questions.explanation: General Pulaski created the Pulaski Cavalry Legion, dying from grape-shot wounds during the 1779 Siege of Savannah.

questions.question: For how many continuous months did the Continental Army remain encamped at Valley Forge between December 1777 and June 1778?
questions.explanation: The army spent six grueling months from December 19, 1777, to June 19, 1778, drilling and regrouping at Valley Forge.

questions.question: Which twin battles in upstate New York in autumn 1777 ended in the surrender of British General John Burgoyne and served as the turning point of the war?
questions.explanation: Burgoyne surrendered his entire army at Saratoga on October 17, 1777, proving to European powers that the Americans could win.

questions.question: Which senior American diplomat spent years in Paris charming French society and securing the vital 1778 Franco-American Treaty of Alliance?
questions.explanation: Benjamin Franklin wit, scientific fame, and rustic charm convinced King Louis XVI to provide open financial and naval aid.

questions.question: Which American general fought heroically at Saratoga before committing infamous treason in 1780 by plotting to surrender West Point to the British?
questions.explanation: Arnold attempted to hand over the West Point fortress to British Major John Andre in exchange for money and a royal commission.

questions.question: In what June 1778 battle in New Jersey did the newly drilled Continental Army fight the British to a tactical draw under blistering summer heat?
questions.explanation: Monmouth proved the effectiveness of Von Steuben's training, featuring the battlefield legend of Molly Pitcher carrying water to artillerymen.

questions.question: Which European kingdom joined the war against Britain in 1779 as an ally of France, capturing British outposts in Florida and Mobile?
questions.explanation: Led by Louisiana Governor Bernardo de Galvez, Spanish forces captured Pensacola and Baton Rouge, opening vital southern supply lines.

questions.question: Approximately how many British, German, and Canadian soldiers formally surrendered with General Burgoyne following the Battles of Saratoga in 1777?
questions.explanation: Burgoyne surrendered roughly 5,800 troops, 27 pieces of artillery, and massive munitions stores to General Horatio Gates.

questions.question: Which Scottish-born naval captain, commanding the Bonhomme Richard, famously shouted that he had not yet begun to fight when asked to surrender?
questions.explanation: Jones fought the heavier British frigate HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head in 1779, capturing her as his own ship sank beneath him.

questions.question: What maritime commerce raiding ships authorized by Congress with letters of marque captured over 600 British merchant vessels during the war?
questions.explanation: Privately owned colonial armed ships seized vital British supplies, severely inflating British shipping insurance rates in London.

questions.question: Which frontier militia leader led daring wilderness campaigns in the Illinois Country, capturing Kaskaskia and Vincennes from the British?
questions.explanation: Clark's winter march through flooded plains secured the Northwest Territory between the Ohio River and the Great Lakes for the United States.

questions.question: Which Mohawk military and political leader allied with the British, leading loyalist and Iroquois raids across the New York frontier?
questions.explanation: Joseph Brant coordinated raids in the Cherry Valley and Mohawk Valley, fiercely resisting American expansion.

questions.question: What major expedition did Washington dispatch in 1779 to destroy forty Iroquois villages aligned with the British in western New York?
questions.explanation: Major General John Sullivan's campaign scorched farmland and orchards, breaking the power of the Iroquois Confederacy.

questions.question: How many naval guns did John Paul Jones flagship Bonhomme Richard carry during its historic 1779 duel against HMS Serapis?
questions.explanation: Originally an East Indiaman merchant vessel, the converted Bonhomme Richard was armed with 42 cannons.

questions.question: Which South Carolina guerrilla commander, known as the Swamp Fox, used hit-and-run tactics against British supply lines in the southern backcountry?
questions.explanation: Francis Marion operated from hidden swamp sanctuaries, frustrating British commander Banastre Tarleton with swift ambushes.

questions.question: Which tactical masterclass in January 1781 saw Brigadier General Daniel Morgan execute a double envelopment to crush Tarleton British Legion in South Carolina?
questions.explanation: Morgan placed militia in the front lines with orders to fire two volleys before falling back, luring British regulars into a devastating trap.

questions.question: Which American general, taking command of the Southern Army in 1780, exhausted Cornwallis through strategic retreat and attritional warfare?
questions.explanation: Nathanael Greene famously declared that his army would rise and fight again, driving British forces out of the Carolinas.

questions.question: Which crucial naval confrontation in September 1781 saw the French fleet under Admiral de Grasse block British naval reinforcement of Yorktown?
questions.explanation: The French victory in the Battle of the Capes prevented the British Royal Navy from evacuating or resupplying Cornwallis' besieged garrison.

questions.question: In what Virginia coastal town did Lord Cornwallis surrender over 7,000 British soldiers on October 19, 1781, effectively ending combat operations?
questions.explanation: Besieged by combined Franco-American armies under Washington and Rochambeau, Cornwallis surrendered as his band played The World Turned Upside Down.

questions.question: In what year CE did General Lord Cornwallis formally surrender his British army at Yorktown, sealing American victory?
questions.explanation: On October 19, 1781, the British capitulation at Yorktown destroyed British parliamentary support for continuing the war.

questions.question: What peace treaty signed in September 1783 formally recognized the independence of the United States and set borders at the Mississippi River?
questions.explanation: Negotiated by John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, and John Jay, the Treaty of Paris doubled the territorial size of the new nation.

questions.question: What was the name of the first written constitution of the United States, adopted in 1777 and ratified in 1781, which established a weak central government?
questions.explanation: The Articles lacked power to tax, regulate interstate commerce, or enforce national laws, leading to financial instability.

questions.question: What armed uprising of debt-burdened Massachusetts farmers between 1786 and 1787 highlighted the weakness of the national government under the Articles?
questions.explanation: Daniel Shays led veterans shutting down county debt courts, alarming leaders like Washington and Madison and spurring the Constitutional Convention.

questions.question: What 1787 legislation established the procedure for admitting new territories into the Union as equal states and banned slavery north of the Ohio River?
questions.explanation: The Northwest Ordinance created a blueprint for orderly western expansion, guaranteeing civil liberties and public education.

questions.question: Where did George Washington resign his military commission in December 1783, establishing civilian supremacy over the armed forces?
questions.explanation: Washington surrendered his sword to Congress at the Maryland State House, establishing a landmark precedent for republican civilian governance.

questions.question: For how many total years were the Articles of Confederation officially in effect as the governing framework of the United States from 1781 to 1789?
questions.explanation: The Articles governed the United States for eight years before being replaced by the United States Constitution in 1789.

questions.question: Who is widely hailed as the Father of the Constitution for authoring the Virginia Plan and keeping detailed notes of the 1787 Constitutional Convention?
questions.explanation: James Madison drafted the Virginia Plan three branches of government and championed the subsequent Bill of Rights amendments.

questions.question: What compromise reached at the Constitutional Convention created a bicameral legislature with proportional House seats and equal Senate representation?
questions.explanation: Proposed by Roger Sherman, the Great Compromise reconciled the interests of large states and small states.

questions.question: What collection of 85 essays arguing in favor of ratifying the US Constitution was written by Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, and John Jay?
questions.explanation: Published under the pseudonym Publius, The Federalist Papers remains the authoritative commentary on the philosophical framework of the Constitution.

questions.question: What first ten amendments to the United States Constitution were ratified in 1791 to guarantee essential individual liberties and state powers?
questions.explanation: Drafted by James Madison to satisfy Anti-Federalist concerns, the Bill of Rights protects freedom of speech, religion, assembly, and trial by jury.

questions.question: Who was unanimously elected by the Electoral College in 1789 to serve as the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: Washington took the first presidential oath of office at Federal Hall in New York City on April 30, 1789, setting foundational executive precedents.

questions.question: How many delegates signed the finished United States Constitution at Independence Hall on September 17, 1787?
questions.explanation: Thirty-nine delegates representing twelve states signed the Constitution, while three present refused to sign without a Bill of Rights.
